summary: AAUW International Fellowships give women who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents a one-year award for full-time study at an accredited U.S. institution: US$20,000 for a first master's and US$25,000 for a doctorate (2027–28 amounts). Since the 2027–28 round it is limited to STEM fields and needs a 3.5/4.0 GPA. Winners are high-achieving women scientists and engineers who are already admitted to a U.S. programme, have a realistic funding plan, and show a real commitment to women and girls and to impact back home.
lookfor: Academic and scholarly excellence (minimum cumulative GPA 3.5 on a 4.0 scale)
Feasibility of your academic, professional or research plan (doctoral: originality and contribution too)
Demonstrated commitment to women and girls
Long-term career goals and commitment to impact
A clear, realistic financial plan showing costs, confirmed and pending funding, and any gap
Preference factors: under-represented country, first international study, living in home country, first-generation graduate, caregiving or single-parent background
cycle: The 2027–28 round ran 17 August – 17 September 2026 (5 pm ET) and is closed; awards are announced in March 2027. Expect the 2028–29 round to open around August 2027 – check the AAUW page from June 2027, and use the year to secure admission and funding plans.

eligibility.q: Do you identify as a woman and are you neither a U.S. citizen nor a U.S. permanent resident (and not applying for a green card)?
eligibility.no: This award is not for you. Consider Fulbright, Chevening, Commonwealth, MEXT, CSC or GKS.

eligibility.q: Will you study a STEM field (science, technology, engineering, maths or medicine) as listed in AAUW's STEM fields document?
eligibility.no: Non-STEM fields are no longer funded from the 2027–28 round. Look at Fulbright, Chevening or university scholarships instead.

eligibility.q: Is your cumulative GPA on your highest degree at least 3.5/4.0 (or a documented equivalent)?
eligibility.no: You are not eligible. A Nigerian First Class or strong Second Class Upper may convert to 3.5+, but check with a credential evaluator before applying.

eligibility.q: Will this be your FIRST master's or FIRST doctorate, studied full time at a U.S. institution accredited by the U.S. Department of Education?
eligibility.no: If you already hold a master's, you can only apply for a doctorate. Part-time, online-only and foreign-branch programmes are not eligible.

eligibility.q: Are you already admitted to (or enrolled in) your U.S. programme when you apply?
eligibility.no: Apply to U.S. universities first (deadlines are often Dec–Feb) and apply to AAUW in the next round once you hold an admission letter.

eligibility.q: Does the programme start by 15 September of the fellowship year and run until at least 30 April?
eligibility.no: Choose a programme start date that fits the fellowship year, or wait one round.

eligibility.q: Have you never received an AAUW fellowship or grant before?
eligibility.no: Previous AAUW fellowship/grant recipients are not eligible (branch awards and Community Action Grants excepted).

steps.title: Confirm you meet every AAUW rule
steps.why: AAUW changed the rules recently (STEM only, 3.5 GPA). An ineligible application is not reviewed.
do: Open the AAUW International Fellowships page and read Eligibility, FAQ and Selection Criteria.
Open the STEM fields PDF and find your exact field name.
Answer each eligibility question in this guide. Stop if any 'must' answer is no.
Note the dates for the round you are targeting.
tips: Check AAUW's historical country profile: it marks Nigeria as a highly represented country, so Nigerians get no 'under-represented country' preference and must win on merit and the other preference factors.
avoid: Using blog posts that still list the old November deadline or non-STEM fields.
check: My field is on the STEM list.
My GPA is 3.5+ on a 4.0 scale.

steps.title: Understand the scoring and plan your funding gap
steps.why: The award is US$20,000–25,000, not full funding. Selectors score how realistic your financial plan is.
do: Write down your programme's full yearly cost: tuition, fees, housing, food, insurance (use the university's cost-of-attendance page).
List funding you have (assistantship, tuition waiver, savings, family, other scholarships) and funding you have applied for.
Calculate the gap after a US$20,000 (master's) or US$25,000 (doctoral) AAUW award.
For each selection criterion, note one piece of evidence from your life.
tips: PhD applicants with a funded assistantship can show AAUW money covers living costs or a dependant – a strong, realistic plan.
check: I know my total cost, my other funding and my gap.

steps.title: Secure admission to your U.S. programme
steps.why: You must be admitted or enrolled when you apply, so U.S. admissions come first.
do: Shortlist up to five accredited U.S. STEM programmes (AAUW lets you list up to five).
Apply before the universities' deadlines, often December–February for the following autumn.
Request application fee waivers where the university offers them.
Save each admission letter as a PDF showing the start date.
tips: If you defer an offer, keep the deferral approval letter – AAUW accepts it with the admission letter.
avoid: Listing a programme you are not admitted to; changing institution or field after the award can disqualify you.
check: I hold at least one admission letter with a start date by 15 September.

steps.title: Build your timeline and create the portal account
steps.why: The application window is short (one month in 2026) and recommenders must also meet the deadline.
do: Note the opening and closing dates when AAUW publishes them (expected around August).
Open the AAUW 'Instructions to create an account' PDF and create your applicant portal account on opening day.
Add milestones: referees asked (opening day), narratives drafted (week 2), uploads done (week 3), submit (3+ days early).
Bookmark the AAUW help desk for technical problems.
tips: Register for AAUW email updates so you see the opening date.
avoid: Starting the portal on the last day.
check: I have a portal account and a written timeline.

links.t: Instructions to create an account in the AAUW applicant portal (PDF)

steps.title: Get official transcripts and proof of degree
steps.why: AAUW requires official transcripts from all degree programmes and proof of a bachelor's-equivalent degree; unofficial copies are rejected.
do: Request official transcripts from every degree programme at your university's Exams & Records office; ask for a sealed or verified electronic copy.
Scan your degree certificates (or provisional statement of result).
If any document is not in English, get a certified English translation.
If your degree title is not clearly bachelor's-equivalent, order a credential evaluation from WES, ECE or another NACES member (allow several weeks and a fee in dollars).
tips: Ask the registry to include your name, degree, courses and grades on the same document; AAUW checks for all four.
check: I have official transcripts for every degree.

steps.title: Prove your GPA on a 4.0 scale
steps.time: about 2 hours (or weeks if using an evaluator)
steps.why: The 3.5 minimum is checked; if your university uses a 5.0 scale or classes of degree, you must document the conversion.
do: Find your cumulative GPA on your transcript (Nigerian universities often use a 5.0 scale).
Convert it with the Scholaro GPA calculator or a credential evaluation, as AAUW's page suggests.
Save the conversion (screenshot or evaluation report) as a PDF.
Use only your highest degree's cumulative GPA.
tips: A WES evaluation is the strongest evidence if your conversion is borderline.
check: I have a document showing 3.5+ on a 4.0 scale.

steps.title: Show English proficiency
steps.time: up to 6 weeks if you need a test
steps.why: AAUW accepts a test score, a native-speaker statement, or a degree from an English-medium institution.
do: If your degree was taught in English (most Nigerian universities), get a transcript or letter stating the language of instruction.
Otherwise, take TOEFL iBT (79+), IELTS (6.5+), Duolingo (120+) or Cambridge (176+).
Upload the official score or the English-medium proof.
tips: Many U.S. universities still require a test even if AAUW does not – check your admission letter.
avoid: Submitting an institutional (in-house) TOEFL score; it is not accepted.
check: I have one accepted form of English evidence.

steps.title: Write your career goals and impact narrative
steps.why: Selectors score your long-term career objectives and the impact you will make, especially at home.
steps.prompt: Explain your career plans and the impact you intend to have (check the portal for the exact wording).
steps.limit: Check the portal; AAUW narrative answers have generally been around 300 words each.
do: State your goal in one sentence: the role you want in 10 years and where.
Give the problem you will solve (e.g. clean water, maternal health, renewable energy in your region) with one fact.
Explain how this U.S. degree builds the exact skills you need.
Name concrete outputs: a lab, a start-up, policy work, teaching girls in STEM.
tips: Short paragraphs and numbers help a reviewer read 300 words fast.
avoid: Big promises with no first step.
check: Each sentence links the degree to the impact.

steps.title: Write your commitment to women and girls
steps.why: This is a scored criterion that many strong scientists treat as an afterthought.
steps.prompt: Show how you have supported, and will support, women and girls (check the portal for the exact wording).
do: List everything you have done: mentoring female students, STEM clubs, women's associations, advocacy, NYSC community projects.
Pick the 1–2 strongest examples and give numbers (how many girls, how long, what changed).
Explain what you will do during and after your degree.
Connect it to your field.
tips: Real, small actions beat vague support for 'gender equality'.
avoid: Writing only about your own struggle without what you did for others.
check: I give at least one concrete example with numbers.

steps.title: Write your academic/research plan and financial plan
steps.why: Feasibility and the financial plan are both scored; doctoral applicants are also judged on originality.
steps.prompt: Describe your programme of study or research and how you will fund it (check the portal for the exact questions).
do: Master's: name the programme, key courses or project and how they fit your goal.
Doctoral: state the research question, method, stage reached and expected contribution.
Financial plan: list costs, confirmed funds, pending funds and the remaining gap, with amounts in US$.
Explain how you will cover any gap.
tips: Use the university's official cost of attendance numbers so your budget is credible.
avoid: A budget that does not add up.
check: My numbers add up and match my admission and aid letters.

steps.title: Get two letters of recommendation
steps.why: Two letters are required and must arrive by the application deadline – late letters make the application incomplete.
do: Choose two people who know your academic or professional work: e.g. your project supervisor and a lecturer or employer.
Ask them as soon as the portal opens; they need professional (institutional) email addresses.
Register them in the portal so they get the upload link.
Send each a one-page brief: your goals, the AAUW criteria, and two examples you want them to mention.
Remind them one week and two days before the deadline.
tips: Ask one referee to speak directly about your work with women and girls.
avoid: Using a dossier service – AAUW does not accept it.
Gmail/Yahoo addresses for referees if an institutional one exists.
check: Both letters show as received in the portal before the deadline.

steps.title: Complete the portal and submit early
steps.why: AAUW states that no late applications are accepted.
do: Fill personal details, citizenship, degrees, GPA, programme(s) and dates.
Upload transcripts, proof of degree, GPA conversion, English proof and admission letter(s).
Paste your proofread narratives.
Check both recommendations are complete.
Submit at least three days before the deadline and save the confirmation.
tips: Read each answer aloud once before submitting.
avoid: Listing a different field or institution from your admission letter.
check: I have a submission confirmation email.

links.t: Watch: AAUW International Fellowship Application Info Session (Dr. ONJY)

steps.title: Wait for results and plan your visa
steps.why: Decisions come in March; AAUW does not sponsor visas, so you must handle your F-1/J-1 through your university.
do: Add AAUW's email to your safe senders and watch for the March decision.
Keep working on your university I-20/DS-2019 and visa interview booking.
If you win, complete AAUW's acceptance process and tax forms (W-8BEN for most international students).
Plan for 14% U.S. tax withholding on the award if you hold an F/J visa (unless a treaty applies).
tips: Use the award letter as proof of funds for your visa interview.
avoid: Changing programme after winning – this can cancel the award.
check: I know when results arrive and what I must do if selected.

steps.title: Report during the fellowship
steps.why: The second payment and good standing depend on reports.
do: Receive the first payment around July–September.
Submit the mid-year report (December) to unlock the second payment.
Submit the final report by 31 July after the fellowship year.
tips: Keep receipts and a short diary of achievements for your reports.
check: Report dates are in my calendar.

faq.a: Not any more. The 2027–28 round closed on 17 September 2026. Expect the next round to open around August 2027.

faq.q: Do I need admission before applying?
faq.a: Yes. You must be admitted or enrolled in your U.S. programme at the time you apply.

faq.q: Does AAUW pay all my costs?
faq.a: No. It pays US$20,000 (master's) or US$25,000 (doctorate) for one year. You need a plan for the rest.

faq.q: I already have a master's. Can I apply for another?
faq.a: No. AAUW funds only your first master's or first doctorate.

faq.q: Can I study outside the U.S.?
faq.a: Only with Graduate Women International membership in limited cases; the main award is for U.S. study.
No. It is a one-year award.
No extra preference: AAUW's country profile lists Nigeria as highly represented. Applicants from under-represented countries get preference.
